purpose: Turn the Noether multilingual workflow into a publishable research/report outline for AI-assisted technical-register construction, interlanguage methodology, educational translation, open-source handoff, and authority boundaries.
working_titles: Auditable AI-assisted technical-register construction for multilingual mathematics
Source shelves before translation: a reproducible workflow for mathematical register transfer
Interlanguage authority and open-source handoff in AI-assisted technical translation
core_thesis: AI-assisted translation can be useful in high-register mathematical contexts only when it is embedded in a workflow that separates mechanical validation, source evidence, terminology governance, render validation, educational usefulness, and native/community authority.
contributions: workflow model for evidence-first technical translation across natural-language, multi-register, zonal/interlanguage, and constructed-pilot lanes
machine-readable artifact discipline for source shelves, term anchors, glossaries, manifests, validation scripts, review packets, and ledgers
claim taxonomy separating mechanical, evidential, pedagogical, community, and canonical-edition claims
terminology-governance model for observed, proposed, approved, sidecar, interlanguage, and constructed-pilot terms
open-source handoff framing that does not equate forkability with community consent
research framing for semi-constructed and interlanguage work under the translation header

article_outline: Introduction: technical-register translation as an authority-sensitive problem
Related work: interlinguistics, language planning, constructed-language pedagogy, OER, FAIR, CARE, TRUST, and open source
Workflow: evidence shelves, term anchors, rendering, manifests, review packets, ledgers
Case study: Noether multilingual lanes and why each lane has different authority gates
Terminology governance: observed terms, proposed terms, approved terms, sidecars, and pilots
Interlanguage methodology: useful bridges, risks, and canonical-edition limits
Educational and open-source handoff: local ownership, forkability, and review boundaries
Results to date: artifact counts, validation state, and unresolved gaps
Limitations: source bias, OCR, licensing, external review, local authority
Conclusion: AI can help build auditable workflows, but cannot confer language authority by itself
